titleEn: Gaṃ is Gaṇeśa. Duṃ is Durgā. Haṃ is Hanumān. The name's first sound, with a hum.
meaningEn: Three seeds you can see through at once: gaṃ is the ga of Gaṇeśa, duṃ the du of Durgā, haṃ the ha of Hanumān — the deity's first sound, closed with a hum. Each opens its deity's short mantra: oṃ gaṃ gaṇapataye namaḥ, oṃ duṃ durgāyai namaḥ, oṃ haṃ hanumate namaḥ. This first-sound logic works for name-seeds like these, and no further. The great seeds — hrīṃ, klīṃ, aiṃ, śrīṃ — are given by the Tantras, not built from a name.
meaningHi: तीन बीज जो एक नज़र में समझ आ जाते हैं: गं गणेश का ग है, दुं दुर्गा का दु, हं हनुमान का ह — देवता की पहली आवाज़, गूँज के साथ बंद। हर एक अपने देवता का छोटा मंत्र खोलता है: ॐ गं गणपतये नमः, ॐ दुं दुर्गायै नमः, ॐ हं हनुमते नमः। पहली-आवाज़ वाला यह हिसाब ऐसे नाम-बीजों पर चलता है, उससे आगे नहीं। बड़े बीज — ह्रीं, क्लीं, ऐं, श्रीं — तंत्रों ने दिए हैं, नाम से नहीं बने।
sayItLike: gum · doom (short 'oo') · hum — each ending in a nasal hum

words.glossEn: Gaṇeśa — the ga of Gaṇa, with a hum
words.glossHi: गणेश — गण का ग, गूँज के साथ
words.root: the one name-seed a text actually derives (Gaṇapati Atharvaśīrṣa §8)

words.glossEn: Durgā — the du of Durgā, with a hum
words.glossHi: दुर्गा — दुर्गा का दु, गूँज के साथ
words.grammar: attested in the Tantras (Śāradā-tilaka, Durgā section); not explained by them

words.glossEn: Hanumān — the ha of Hanumān, with a hum
words.glossHi: हनुमान — हनुमान का ह, गूँज के साथ
words.grammar: attested in Mantra-mahodadhi (Hanumat section). The same sound is also the space-element seed in the cakra map — one syllable, two traditional uses

source.text: Gaṇapati Atharvaśīrṣa §8 (gaṃ); Śāradā-tilaka Tantra, Durgā paṭala (duṃ); Mantra-mahodadhi (1588), Hanumat taraṅga (haṃ)
source.ref: gaṃ is derived at Atharvaśīrṣa §8; duṃ and haṃ are given, not derived, in the tantric handbooks
source.note: Only gaṃ is explained by a text. Duṃ and haṃ are attested but not derived; the 'first sound' pattern is something a learner can see, not a rule the Tantras state.

significance.textSays: Atharvaśīrṣa §8: ga + a + ṃ is the Gaṇeśa-vidyā. The Śāradā-tilaka and Mantra-mahodadhi simply hand over duṃ for Durgā and haṃ for Hanumān.
significance.traditionSays: Each of the three opens its deity's short mantra: oṃ gaṃ gaṇapataye namaḥ · oṃ duṃ durgāyai namaḥ · oṃ haṃ hanumate namaḥ. Haṃ doubles, in a different use, as the seed of space in the cakra map.
significance.weDoNotClaim: That first-sound is a rule to extend. It fits name-seeds; hrīṃ, klīṃ, aiṃ and śrīṃ are not made this way.

practice.timeOfDay: as part of the deity's mantra, not alone

quiz.prompt: Which of these seeds is NOT built from the deity's first sound?
Only one name-seed is actually derived by a text. Which?
